instructions: Assess only the listed primary candidates in a fresh invocation. Read their dialogue first, then the exact card; use the alternate only to judge meaningful differentiation. Supply six criterion ratings with specific turn evidence and full coach-2.0 findings. Do not invent missing backstory or assume earlier approval. No writer scores or rationales are supplied. Report real reservations and failures. Totals are calculated in code.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

card.title: Exactly as Planned
card.instruction: Treat every exposed flaw, failed step, and unexpected consequence as proof that the scheme is unfolding by design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The escape-room attendant found our shortcut. Phase one is working.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made me distract her so you could crawl through it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She was supposed to feel she'd caught us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's throwing us out. We haven't solved a single clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the fast exit I planned. Ask her to put our time on the leaderboard; solving clues was only our cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum found the surprise-party invitations. Right on schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made me hide them in my sock drawer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She had to feel she'd uncovered it herself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's cancelling the caterer. She hates surprises.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's her part of the plan: taking control. We surprise her with how completely we obey.

card.title: I Know the Procedure
card.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll investigate the missing raffle tin. Naturally, we begin with access.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cleaner has the only cupboard key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As expected. Where does our keyholder go after cleaning?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception. But the tin never went in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we've eliminated that location. Confirm where you last saw it; I'll establish our next search area.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As building manager, I'll establish why this door won't lock. Describe the anomaly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hinge is loose. I usually tighten it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely. Show me your usual method so I can assess it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll need the screwdriver from your desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, we've reached the tool stage. Which drawer do you normally find it in?

card.title: Outsmart the Room
card.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open the delivery email. Let me deduce where our office biscuits went.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for them. I'll tell everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait. That's a clue, not a conclusion. I should announce the solution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. They're downstairs opening the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them nobody eats until I identify the contents. Finding a box doesn't mean they've solved the biscuits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my conclusion above yours on the board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're the same conclusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then chronology decides who outsmarted whom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We spoke together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My chalk reached the board first.

card.title: The Plan Gets Better
card.instruction: Celebrate every setback as proof that the scheme is becoming more sophisticated, selective, or impossible to detect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The alley's blocked. Excellent: our secret proposal picnic just got harder to discover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm carrying your table. We have to use the main road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better camouflage. Everyone will assume we're moving house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your girlfriend's coming down the road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Now she can carry the chairs without suspecting romance. The disguise gets more convincing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only six people cracked our supper-club invitation. Excellent: a more selective table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Five thought it was a puzzle night. They've cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. We've filtered out everyone who wasn't committed to dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The last one's the printer asking to be paid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An invitation-only dinner with our sole supplier. It's become a private partnership event.
